notes:
- The palette lives on the title page: A palette button on a title's Info page opens a full-height appearance editor over the page itself. A miniature of the page updates as you pick a backdrop, blur and tint, so you choose by looking at the result instead of a swatch in Settings. The editor is also on the docked bar once the hero has scrolled away, and every choice still lives in Settings > Theme.
- Anime and manga search are separate: The Search page asks one namespace at a time, with an Anime/Manga switch under the field. Settings > Library > Bottom bar has independent Anime search and Manga search switches; turning one off removes it from the page, and turning both off hides the Search tab and its top-bar shortcut instead of opening an empty page. This also keeps anime id 1 and manga id 1 from sharing a result card.
- Home shows a cover from your own shelf: The Anime List card now takes its artwork from your own in-progress or recently updated anime, and the Manga List card draws from a small page of your most recently updated manga instead of one fixed poster. Each visit can show a different cover, and the existing queries supply it with no extra request.
- A tint for the title page: The Info page backdrop gained a Natural/Tinted choice. Tinted blends the active theme accent into the blurred artwork below the legibility scrim, so a grey or brown key visual still belongs to the app around it. It sits beside Backdrop and Softness in both the in-page editor and Settings > Theme.
- The bottom bar switches stay honest: The catalogue controls now follow one set of rules, so the Search tab, its top-bar shortcut and the two namespace switches cannot disagree about whether the page has anything to search.
